name: O an quan
shortDescription: Sow stones around the board and capture villagers and mandarins. Most points when both mandarins are gone wins.
rules:
The board has 10 villager squares (5 per side, 5 stones each) and 2 mandarin squares at the ends. A mandarin is worth **10 stones**. Side 1 moves first.

On your turn, pick one of **your** squares that has stones and a direction. Take all its stones and sow them one per square in that direction.

After the last stone, look at the next square: if it has **stones**, pick them up and keep sowing; if it is a **mandarin square**, your turn ends; if it is **empty**, **capture** everything in the square after it. After a capture, if you meet another empty square followed by a full one, **capture again**. Two empty squares in a row end your turn.

If all 5 of your squares are empty at the start of your turn, 5 of your captured stones are put back, one per square; if you have fewer, you **borrow** from your opponent and pay back when scoring.

The game ends when **both mandarins have been captured**. Stones left on your squares are yours. Most points wins.
